subject.title: exec auto-reviewer re-bills a fresh model completion for every byte-identical repeated exec

question: Should OpenClaw reuse model-backed exec reviewer decisions for byte-identical requests within one reviewer instance, and what cache key/outcome scope is acceptable for the exec approval boundary?
rationale: The source-level cost bug is real, but the fix deliberately changes one-request-one-review semantics for process execution approvals, so the cache contract needs maintainer intent before closing or auto-repairing.

options.title: Approve full-input per-run memo
options.body: Cache reviewer decisions only inside one reviewer instance and key the cache by the exact serialized reviewed input or prompt, without converting results into durable approval state.

options.title: Narrow cached outcomes
options.body: Cache only parsed low-risk allow-once results, or key by an even stricter prompt hash, if maintainers want a smaller security-boundary change.

options.title: Keep fresh-review semantics
options.body: Reject memoization for now and accept repeated reviewer cost to preserve a fresh model review for every exec approval miss.

recommendation.title: Approve full-input per-run memo
recommendation.body: Cache reviewer decisions only inside one reviewer instance and key the cache by the exact serialized reviewed input or prompt, without converting results into durable approval state.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the merged normalized exec auto mode feature and is the strongest current routing signal for the approval-boundary cache decision.
